newsitem.title: UK: UK SIB says pensions review to take in ACT change.
newsitem.headline: UK SIB says pensions review to take in ACT change.

text.p: British financial watchdog the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said on Friday it would take into account changes to advanced corporation tax (ACT) recovery in calculating compensation for victims of pensions mis-selling.

"The basis for calculating prospective loss and redress in pension transfer and opt out cases will be revised to take account of the abolition of ACT recovery for pension funds," it said in a statement.
SIB said the revised basis for calculating loss and redress would be contained in the next quarterly review of rates of return, which would be published as scheduled on August 1.
"This review will also take account of changes in investment conditions during the current quarter, including interest rates, inflation rates and returns on equities and gilts," it added.
The adjustment in respect of ACT will be backdated to July 2, the date of the budget when the change was announced by Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown.
Calculations of loss and offers made by firms on or after that date will need to be amended to take the abolition of ACT recovery into account, SIB said.
The watchdog again warned pensions companies to get on with processing cases of pensions mis-selling "which have yet to reach the stage where prospective loss or redress needs to be calcluated".

More than half a million people may have been wrongly advised to take out personal pensions instead of staying with occupational schemes between 1988 and 1994 and regulators have moved to speed up compensation payments to those who lost out.

In 1994, SIB told the pension industry to undertake a widespread review of all personal pensions sold between the end of April 1988 and the end of June 1994. Since then, firms involved have been set a target deadline of 1998 to complete all cases.
